question.problem:
Find the radius of convergence $R$ for the series

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(3x-6)^{n}}{(n!)^{2}}=(3x-6)+\frac{(3x-6)^{2}}{(2!)^{2}}+\frac{(3x-6)^{3}}{(3!)^{2}}+⋯\,.
$$

$R=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
To apply the ratio test, we define ${a}_{n}=\frac{(3x-6)^{n}}{(n!)^{2}}.$ Then, we calculate the ratio of two successive terms and take the limit as $n\to \infty :$

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{a}_{n+1}}{{a}_{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{\frac{(3x-6)^{n+1}}{((n+1)!)^{2}}}{\frac{(3x-6)^{n}}{(n!)^{2}}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{(3x-6)^{n+1}}{((n+1)!)^{2}}\cdot \frac{(n!)^{2}}{(3x-6)^{n}}| \\  & =|3x-6|{lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{1}{(n+1)^{2}} \\  & =|3x-6|\cdot 0 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The series converges if $L<1.$ In this case, the convergence condition is satisfied for all $-\infty <x<\infty .$ Therefore, we conclude that the radius of convergence is $R=\infty .$
